SMTO-CFG-0037 — SMTO's settings file has a formatting mistake

GUID: 2dc0250d-2791-4c9c-8b91-9cf724b662a6
Slug: config-invalid-app-config-yaml-at
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't read its startup settings file (usually config.yaml) because the text isn't laid out the way it expects, so it stopped. The file wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the settings file named in the message in a plain text editor and go to the line the message mentions. The message points to where SMTO stopped understanding the file; the mistake is usually on that line or just above it.
  2. Check that area for common slips: tabs instead of spaces, uneven indentation, a missing colon after a setting name, or a quote that isn't closed. The file uses spaces and colons to show which value belongs to which setting, so one slip breaks the layout.
  3. If you can't spot the mistake, put back the last copy of the file that worked, then start SMTO again. A known-good copy lets SMTO start while the new change is checked separately.

What success looks like

  • SMTO starts and the startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full message and send it with the file, after removing any passwords or API keys, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep starting SMTO with the same file; it stops at the same place every time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Bootstrap configuration loading failed because yaml.safe_load raised a YAMLError while parsing the selected application configuration file.

What this means

  • yaml.safe_load raises YAMLError while loading the selected application configuration file. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • yaml.safe_load raises YAMLError while loading the selected application configuration file.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the parser's safe location detail and YAML structure without copying private configuration values into diagnostics.

How to fix it

  • Open the file path shown in the message and fix the YAML syntax error reported by yaml.safe_load (the message includes the line and column). The file must parse to a top-level mapping of config_version, server, llm, runtime and sql; validate it with aor doctor --config before restarting.
  • Correct the YAML syntax and use a top-level mapping in the application configuration. Keep private values in their supported configuration fields.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended file parses successfully before typed configuration validation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
